subject.title: fix embedded compaction hook reset API

question: Should OpenClaw expose a supported `after_compaction` hook API that can request a deferred reset of the current session, rather than keeping this recovery behavior private to an owner plugin or existing lifecycle seam?
rationale: The branch changes the plugin-facing hook context with a new lifecycle capability, and code review cannot determine the permanent supported contract or owner boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve a narrow hook contract
options.body: Keep the API limited to successful, resettable after-compaction contexts, document its deferred current-session semantics, and require the remaining cron repair and current-head proof.

options.title: Keep reset ownership private
options.body: Remove the plugin-facing API and implement any compaction-reset policy in the owning plugin or core lifecycle until a broader hook contract is designed.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow hook contract
recommendation.body: Keep the API limited to successful, resettable after-compaction contexts, document its deferred current-session semantics, and require the remaining cron repair and current-head proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged session-state compatibility work makes this the best available routing candidate for the lifecycle and persistence decision.
